docs.title: boxes-backed State-Machine Visualizer
docs.text: sysmlpy.boxes_view is an optional renderer that produces a boxes Diagram from a parsed SysML v2 state def. It complements as_state_transition_view() (the PlantUML renderer) by producing native UML shapes — rounded-corner «state» boxes, filled-circle initial pseudostate, bullseye final state, orthogonal port-to-port routing — without needing a Java runtime or a PlantUML server.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
boxes is an optional dependency. From the sysmlpy checkout:

poetry run pip install -e ../boxes

or, if you have boxes on PyPI / a wheel:

pip install boxes

import sysmlpy keeps working without boxes installed — the new symbols are lazy-loaded on first access and raise an informative ImportError if boxes is missing.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
import sysmlpy

# Build an in-memory boxes.Diagram you can introspect or further decorate
d = sysmlpy.as_state_transition_view_boxes(model, focus=None)

# Render straight to the terminal (braille characters)
print(sysmlpy.render_state_transition_view(model, routing="orthogonal"))

# Render to an SVG string
svg = sysmlpy.render_state_transition_view_svg(model, routing="orthogonal")
open("state.svg", "w").write(svg)

model accepts raw SysML text, a sysmlpy.Model, or the dict from sysmlpy.load_grammar(). focus chooses a specific state def by name when multiple are present in the same source.

The pseudostate shape classes are re-exported so diagram-author code can use the state-machine vocabulary directly:

from sysmlpy.boxes_view import (
    InitialPseudostate, JunctionPseudostate,
    ChoicePseudostate, ForkPseudostate, JoinPseudostate,
    FinalState, TerminatePseudostate,
    HistoryPseudostate, EntryPoint, ExitPoint, StateNode,
)

docs.title: What the adapter handles
docs.text:
The adapter walks the visitor dict and emits one round-cornered StateNode per state X declaration, one InitialPseudostate (filled black circle) for entry; then X;, and one FinalState (bullseye) the first time a transition targets the reserved done name. Transitions are emitted as edges labelled with Trigger [guard].

SysML v2 construct Adapter output state def X { … } one diagram per state def (use focus= to choose) entry; then X; InitialPseudostate → edge (no arrowhead) → first state state A; StateNode with «state» stereotype, rounded corners entry action warmup : WarmUp; / do monitor; / exit act; attributes entry / warmup, do / monitor, exit / act in the state box transition T first A accept Trig if guard do Effect then B; one edge A → B with label Trig [guard] accept X then Y; (shorthand succession) synthesized transition with trigger X, target Y, source back-filled from the most-recently declared state in the region transition first A accept X then done; edge to a synthesized FinalState bullseye (one per region, reused if multiple transitions hit done) transition first A accept X then S2.S3; full feature-chain resolution — endpoint correctly identified as the nested substate S2.S3 state Composite { state A; state B; transition first A accept X then B; } composite state emitted as a StateNode; substates emitted as namespace-qualified siblings (Composite.A, Composite.B). Recursive — supports arbitrary nesting depth state R parallel { state A; state B; } (isParallel=true) composite state carries both «state» and «parallel» stereotypes

docs.title: The SysML v2 pseudostate landscape
docs.text:
The UML / SysML 1.x menagerie of pseudostates — initial, final, terminate, junction, choice, fork, join, shallow-history, deep-history, entry-point, exit-point — was deliberately collapsed in SysML v2. The formal spec (formal/26-03-02, Sept 2025, §7.18) keeps only:

  • Initial — not a named shape; expressed as a succession from the state's (possibly empty) entry action: entry; then X;
  • Final — the reserved transition target done. Spec §7.18: "a transition to done indicates that the source state is the final state of the containing state performance."
  • Parallel — the parallel keyword on a StateDefBody marks orthogonal regions composition (no transitions allowed between concurrent substates)
  • Guarded choice — UML 1.x's choice and junction pseudostates are replaced by if guard then target conditional successions

The following UML 1.x / SysML 1.x state pseudostates have no token in the lexer, no production in the grammar, and no class in the Ecore metamodel, and are correspondingly not emitted by the adapter:

Removed pseudostate What replaces it in SysML v2 Junction guarded transitions Choice if guard then target conditional successions Shallow history (none — not in the language) Deep history (none — not in the language) Entry point (none — composite states are entered directly) Exit point (none — composite states are exited directly) Terminate done (final) covers the common case Fork / Join moved to action flow (fork-node, join-node in §8.2.2.14.1), not state machines

The boxes package still ships first-class JunctionPseudostate, ChoicePseudostate, ForkPseudostate, JoinPseudostate, HistoryPseudostate, EntryPoint, ExitPoint, TerminatePseudostate classes so you can build SysML 1.x / UML-style diagrams by hand when you need them — they just aren't emitted by the SysML v2 adapter because the source language has no equivalent input.

docs.title: Example: the OMG StateTest.sysml state machine
docs.text:
import sysmlpy

text = """state def S {
    entry; then S1;
    state S1;
        accept s : Sig then S2;
    state S2 { state S3; }
    accept Exit then done;
    transition
        first S1
        accept s : Sig
        then S2.S3;
}"""

print(sysmlpy.render_state_transition_view(text, routing="orthogonal"))

The output is a braille-character diagram showing:

  • a filled black circle (initial pseudostate)
  • a «state» S1 box → «state» S2 (with shorthand accept s : Sig edge)
  • a «state» S3 substate (sibling of S2 visually; nesting is a future layout enhancement)
  • a «state» S1 → «state» S3 edge for the explicit transition first S1 … then S2.S3
  • an Exit edge from S1 (the most-recent declared state at that point in the region) to a bullseye final state

Use render_state_transition_view_svg(...) to produce a vector SVG instead, suitable for embedding in docs or editing by hand.

docs.title: Limitations / future work
docs.text:
• Composite nesting is currently visual-sibling, not visuallyenclosed — boxes lays out substates as top-level nodes with namespace-qualified names (Composite.A). True UML "substates inside the parent box" rendering builds on the View.children infrastructure in boxes and is a focused future enhancement.
  • Edge labels are best-effort — complex guard expressions other than a single QualifiedName are currently dropped to keep the diagram readable. Trivial to extend if needed.
  • state usage (top-level state x :> StateDef parallel { … }) — parsed fine, but the adapter currently only descends into StateDefinition bodies. A small extension handles StateUsage top-level — beyond what the typical state-machine test fixture exercises.

docs.title: How-to: SysML v2 in Jupyter with the %%sysml magic
docs.text: Write SysML v2 textual notation directly in notebook cells, keep a live model in the session, query it from Python, and render PlantUML views — powered by sysmlpy, with no JVM and no separate kernel install.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pip install "sysmlpy[jupyter]"
# or, with the Poetry/uv project you are working in:
#   poetry add "sysmlpy[jupyter]"      /      uv add "sysmlpy[jupyter]"

The extra pulls in IPython ≥ 8. Everything else (parser, analyzer, PlantUML generators) ships in sysmlpy core. JupyterLab/Jupyter Notebook itself is assumed present (or install sysmlpy[jupyter] alongside your normal jupyterlab install).

docs.title: 2. Load the extension
docs.text:
In the first cell of a notebook:

%load_ext sysmlpy.ipython_magic

Successful load prints nothing. (If it errors with No module named IPython, the jupyter extra is missing.)

docs.title: 3. Your first SysML cell
docs.text:
A %%sysml cell contains SysML v2 textual notation, not Python:

%%sysml
package Vehicle {
    part def Engine {
        attribute fuelRate : Real;
    }
    part def Vehicle {
        part engine : Vehicle::Engine;
    }
}

Output:

sysml: model updated — 1 package(s) loaded

The parsed model is persistent across cells and bound into the notebook namespace as model (alias _sysml). Verify from a normal Python cell:

[p.name for p in model.packages]      # ['Vehicle']
model.find(name="Engine")             # exact declared-name search, any depth
engine = model.find(name="Engine", sysml_type="part")[0]
[a.name for a in engine.attributes]   # ['fuelRate']
model                                 # rich collapsible tree display

Name-lookup note: find/find_one match an element's declared name, exactly, anywhere in the tree — :: in a query is not interpreted as a path. If a package and a part share a name (package Vehicle { part def Vehicle; }), disambiguate with the type filter (model.find(name="Vehicle", sysml_type="package") vs sysml_type="part"), or navigate structurally from a unique anchor (model.find_one("Engine").parent), or use model.path_between(src, dst) / model.traverse(cb) for path-shaped queries. find_one raises LookupError rather than guessing when a name is ambiguous — treat that as a feature and narrow the query.

docs.title: 4. The iteration workflow
docs.text:
The natural loop is one %%sysml cell per element you are working on. Re-declaring a package merges at package-member granularity: an element with the same name + sysml_type replaces the prior definition; sibling members are preserved.

%%sysml
package Vehicle {
    part def Vehicle {
        part engine : Vehicle::Engine;
        attribute mass : Real = 1500;
    }
}

sysml: model updated — 1 package(s) loaded, 1 redefined

part def Engine is still in the model — only part def Vehicle was replaced. Parse errors are reported to stderr with line/column and never discard the session model; fix the cell and re-run.

Options on the %%sysml line:

Option Effect --reset Discard the session model before parsing this cell --file PATH Parse SysML from a file instead of the cell body (use - as the cell body) --show Print the round-tripped (canonicalized) model text after merging

docs.title: 5. Querying and visualizing
docs.text:
Line magics (modeled on the OMG Pilot Implementation Jupyter kernel command set):

%sysml_reset                 # discard the session model
%sysml_list                  # list top-level packages
%sysml_list Engine           # elements matching an exact declared name
%sysml_show Engine           # AST dump rooted at a named element
%sysml_show Engine --json    # JSON representation when the dump parses
%sysml_viz Vehicle           # PlantUML view (default: general)
%sysml_viz Vehicle --view tree

%sysml_viz views: general, interconnection, action, package, tree. Output is PlantUML text; render it with the PlantUML CLI, the VS Code PlantUML extension, or a PlantUML server — e.g. paste into https://www.plantuml.com/plantuml.

For anything richer, drop into Python — the model is a live object:

model.find(sysml_type="part", recursive=False)   # top-level parts only
model.find(name="Engine")[0].attributes
pkg = model.find_one("Vehicle")
list(pkg)                                        # children

docs.title: 6. Semantic diagnostics
docs.text:
After each successful merge, sysmlpy's semantic analyzer runs best-effort over the session model. Issues print to stderr as:

[semantic] [CODE] message

These are advisory (the model is still merged); use sysml-style check sysml/models/*.sysml in CI for hard gating.

docs.title: 7. Saving your work
docs.text:
The magic edits the in-memory model. To persist back to .sysml files, use --show to see canonical text and paste it into your model files, or run the formatter from the shell:

sysmlpy format sysml/models/*.sysml

To package a model directory for interchange, see the .kpar packaging how-to in the sysml-copier template (scripts/make_kpar.py in generated projects).

docs.title: 8. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix No module named IPython Install the extra: pip install "sysmlpy[jupyter]" %%sysml is a cell magic, but the cell body is empty IPython requires a body; with --file, put - in the body find_one: 2 matches for 'X' X names both a package and an element — use a qualified name or model.find(name=..., sysml_type=...) unknown view '...' %sysml_viz --view accepts general|interconnection|action|package|tree Session model looks stale/corrupted %sysml_reset, then re-run your definition cells Diagrams show as raw PlantUML text Render with PlantUML (CLI/server/extension); the magic emits text by design

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide explains sysmlpy through working examples derived from the test suite.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
::

pip install sysmlpy

Or from source::

pip install -e .

docs.title: Basic Workflow
docs.text:
sysmlpy provides two-way translation between SysML v2 text and Python objects:

  1. Parse SysML text → Python object using loads()
  2. Build Python object → SysML text using .dump()

::

from sysmlpy import loads

# Parse text to Python
text = "package Rocket;"
model = loads(text)

# Python to text
output = model.dump()
# → "package Rocket;"

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Create a package::

from sysmlpy import Package

p = Package(name="Rocket")
print(p.dump())
# → "package Rocket;"

Package with body::

p = Package(name="Rocket")
p.add_child(Package(name="Engine"))
print(p.dump())
# → package Rocket {
#        package Engine;
#     }

Short names (alias IDs)::

p = Package(name="Rocket", shortname="'3.1'")
print(p.dump())
# → package <'3.1'> Rocket;

docs.title: Items
docs.text:
Create an item usage::

from sysmlpy import Item

i = Item(name="Fuel")
print(i.dump())
# → item Fuel;

Item definition::

i = Item(definition=True, name="Fuel")
print(i.dump())
# → item def Fuel;

Items with children::

i = Item(name="Fuel")
i.add_child(Item(name="Oxidizer"))
print(i.dump())
# → item Fuel {
#        item Oxidizer;
#     }

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
Parts work like items::

from sysmlpy import Part

p = Part(name="Engine")
print(p.dump())
# → part Engine;

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attributes with values::

from sysmlpy import Attribute, ureg

a = Attribute(name="mass")
a.set_value(100 * ureg.kilogram)
print(a.dump())
# → attribute mass = 100 [kilogram];

Composite structures::

from sysmlpy import Part, Attribute

p = Part(name="Stage1")
p.add_child(Attribute(name="mass"))
p.add_child(Attribute(name="thrust"))
print(p.dump())
# → part Stage1 {
#        attribute mass;
#        attribute thrust;
#     }

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Actions (activities) can be defined with input and output parameters::

from sysmlpy import Action

# Action definition with typed inputs/outputs
a = Action(definition=True, name='Focus')
a.add_input('scene', 'Scene')
a.add_output('image', 'Image')
print(a.dump())
# → action def Focus { in scene : Scene; out image : Image; }

# Action usage with references
b = Action(name='TakePicture')
b.add_input('scene')
b.add_output('picture')
print(b.dump())
# → action TakePicture { in scene; out picture; }

docs.title: References
docs.text:
References can reference other elements::

from sysmlpy import Reference, Item

# Simple reference
r = Reference(name='driver')
print(r.dump())
# → ref driver;

# Reference with type
person = Item(name='Person')
r2 = Reference(name='driver')
r2.set_type(person)
print(r2.dump())
# → ref driver : Person;

# Reference redefinition
r3 = Reference(name='payload', redefines=True)
r3.set_type(person)
print(r3.dump())
# → ref :>> payload : Person;

docs.title: Typing (Subclassing)
docs.text:
An item can be typed by a definition::

from sysmlpy import Item

# Create definition
fuel_def = Item(definition=True, name="Fuel")

# Create usage typed by definition
hydrogen = Item(name="Hydrogen")
hydrogen.set_typed_by(fuel_def)
print(hydrogen.dump())
# → item Hydrogen : Fuel;

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
A Model contains packages::

from sysmlpy import Model, Package

m = Model()
m.add_child(Package(name="Rocket"))
m.add_child(Package(name="Payload"))
print(m.dump())
# → package Rocket;
#     package Payload;

docs.title: Loading full text
docs.text:
Parse complete SysML text::

from sysmlpy import loads

text = """package Rocket {
       item def Fuel;
       item Hydrogen : Fuel;
    }"""

model = loads(text)
print(model.dump())

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: For more examples, see the test files in tests/class_test.py.

docs.title: Python Representation
docs.text:
All classes have __repr__ that returns constructor-style output::

from sysmlpy import Package, Item, Part, Attribute, Action, Reference

p = Package(name='Rocket')
print(repr(p))
# → Package(name='Rocket')

i = Item(definition=True, name='Fuel')
print(repr(i))
# → Item(definition=True, name='Fuel')

part = Part(name='Engine')
print(repr(part))
# → Part(name='Engine')

attr = Attribute(name='mass')
print(repr(attr))
# → Attribute(name='mass')

Anonymous elements show a UUID until named::

from sysmlpy import Package
p = Package()
print(repr(p))
# → Package(name='a1b2c3d4-...')  # UUID

docs.title: Storage Backends
docs.text:
sysmlpy provides a unified storage protocol with multiple backends::

from sysmlpy.store import create_store

# In-memory (default, zero dependencies)
store = create_store("memory")

# NetworkX graph (analysis, shortest paths, centrality)
store = create_store("networkx")

# Kuzu embedded graph DB (disk persistence, Cypher queries)
store = create_store("kuzu", database="/tmp/model.db")

# Cayley remote graph DB (HTTP API, BoltDB/LevelDB backends)
store = create_store("cayley", host="localhost", port=64210)

All backends share the same API::

from sysmlpy.store import new_id

eid = new_id()
store.put(eid, {"name": "Engine", "sysml_type": "part"})
data = store.get(eid)       # → {"name": "Engine", "sysml_type": "part"}
store.has(eid)              # → True
store.delete(eid)           # → True

# Query elements
results = store.query(sysml_type="part")
results = store.query(name="Engine*")  # wildcard

# Graph traversal
store.descendants(root_id)
store.ancestors(leaf_id)
store.path(source_id, target_id)

CayleyStore communicates with a running Cayley server over HTTP, storing elements as quads (subject, predicate, object, label). Run Cayley with Docker::

# In-memory backend
docker run -p 64210:64210 --rm cayley/cayley

# Persistent BoltDB backend
docker run -p 64210:64210 -v /data:/data --rm cayley/cayley -db boltdb -dbpath /data/cayley.db

docs.title: Multi-File Projects
docs.text:
sysmlpy supports loading multiple SysML files into a shared model with automatic cross-file import resolution.

Load multiple files::

from sysmlpy import load_files, analyze

model = load_files([
    'models/Shared/Types.sysml',
    'models/SystemGateway/SystemGatewayMain.sysml',
])
issues = analyze(model)

Packages with the same name are automatically merged::

# types1.sysml: package Types { part def Engine; }
# types2.sysml: package Types { part def Wheel; }
model = load_files(['types1.sysml', 'types2.sysml'])
# Both Engine and Wheel are in the same Types package

Load an entire project directory::

from sysmlpy import load_project

# Load all .sysml and .kerml files recursively
model = load_project('models/')

# Load from an entry point (only reachable files)
model = load_project('models/', entry='models/main.sysml')

Load a file with automatic dependency resolution::

from sysmlpy import load_with_dependencies

model = load_with_dependencies(
    'models/SystemGateway/SystemGatewayMain.sysml',
    search_paths=['models/SystemGateway', 'models/Shared'],
)

Standard library imports (ScalarValues, ISQ, etc.) are validated when a library path is provided::

import sysmlpy
library_path = '/path/to/sysmlpy/library'
model = load_files(['main.sysml'], library=library_path)

docs.title: PlantUML View Renderings
docs.text:
sysmlpy provides 17 view rendering functions for generating diagrams from parsed SysML v2 models. All default to black-and-white output suitable for journal articles, and accept focus=, style="color", and custom_style= parameters.

Standard view functions (PlantUML output)::

from sysmlpy.plantuml import (
    as_graphical_rendering,     # Elements + relationship arrows
    as_general_view,            # GV — most general view
    as_package_view,            # Package hierarchy
    as_interconnection_diagram, # IV — connectors and flows
    as_action_flow_view,        # AFV — action flows
    as_state_transition_view,   # STV — state machines
    as_tree_diagram,            # Nested containment tree
    as_element_table,           # Tabular element listing
    as_textual_notation,        # Indented text notation
)

model = sysmlpy.loads("package P { part def Engine { port intake; } }")

# General View: all elements as a graph of nodes and edges
print(as_general_view(model))

# Action Flow View: actions with control/object flows
print(as_action_flow_view(model))

# State Transition View: hierarchical state machines
print(as_state_transition_view(model))

GridView specializations (PlantUML / Markdown / HTML output)::

from sysmlpy.plantuml import (
    as_tabular_view,                # Configurable columns
    as_data_value_tabular_view,     # Attribute values + units
    as_relationship_matrix_view,    # Pairwise relationship matrix
)

# Markdown table for docs
print(as_tabular_view(model, output_format="markdown"))

# HTML table with CSS classes
print(as_data_value_tabular_view(model, output_format="html"))

# Relationship matrix with type filtering
print(as_relationship_matrix_view(model, row_type="part",
                                  output_format="markdown"))

All rendering functions accept style="color" for colored output and custom_style for user-defined PlantUML style overrides::

puml = as_tree_diagram(model, custom_style=[
    'skinparam defaultFontSize 14',
    'skinparam rectangle { LineThickness 2.5 }',
])

See the README for rendered examples of all 16 view types: docs/plantuml-examples/.

docs.title: Stylistic Checks
docs.text:
The analyze() function now includes stylistic checks that warn about naming convention violations and file-package mismatches::

from sysmlpy import loads, analyze

model = loads("package mypkg { part def engine; }")

# Default: stylistic checks enabled
issues = analyze(model)
# → NAMING_CONVENTION warnings for 'mypkg', 'engine'

# With filename check
issues = analyze(model, filename="Engine.sysml")
# → FILE_PACKAGE_MISMATCH warning for 'mypkg' vs 'Engine'

# Disable stylistic checks
issues = analyze(model, style_checks=False)

Naming conventions enforced:

  • Definitions (part def, action def, etc.): PascalCase (Engine)
  • Usages (part, action, etc.): camelCase (myEngine)
  • Packages: PascalCase (MyPackage)
  • Attributes: camelCase (powerLevel)
  • Ports: camelCase (intakePort)

All stylistic issues have severity "warning" rather than "error", so they don't block validation but still highlight potential issues. Specialization Keywords on Usages (v0.40.0+)

All four SysML v2 specialization kinds round-trip on any usage — attributes, parts, actions, requirements, and more::

from sysmlpy import loads

model = loads("""package P {
    action a1 :> BaseType;
    action a2 ::> RefType;
    action a3 references OtherType;   # keyword form
    action a4 :>> RedefType;
}""")

print(model.dump())
# action a1:>BaseType ;
# action a2::> R ;
# ... (keyword form canonicalizes to the operator form)

docs.title: Redeclared Feature Names (v0.39.0+)
docs.text:
When a usage re-declares a feature without its own identification, the user-visible name lives in the specialization chain. Two helpers surface it::

from sysmlpy import loads

model = loads("""package P {
    view def V :> Base {
        attribute :>> exampleAttribute = "Example Value";
    }
}""")
attr = model.get_child("P.V").attributes[0]

print(attr.redefined_name)   # → exampleAttribute
print(attr.display_name)     # → exampleAttribute (UUID-aware)
print(attr.get_value())      # → Example Value

self.name stays the auto-generated UUID sentinel for backward compatibility; display_name suppresses it for UI / log output.

docs.title: Partial Parse Recovery (v0.38.0+)
docs.text:
Keep whatever did parse when the input has syntax errors::

from sysmlpy import load_partial, PartialParseError
from sysmlpy.formatting import classtree

try:
    model = load_partial(text)
except PartialParseError as e:
    print(e.errors)              # collected ANTLR errors
    print(classtree(e.partial).dump())  # valid part of the input

The strict loads / load are unchanged.

docs.title: State-Machine Simulation (sysmlpy sim)
docs.text:
Cameo-style simulation for SysML v2 state def machines: the model's machine becomes executable — triggers fire transitions, guards are evaluated for real against the model's attribute values (pint-aware, via the v0.64 expression evaluator), effects are logged, and the live state is shown while you drive.

Requires the optional sim extra:

poetry install -E sim          # or: pip install 'sysmlpy[sim]'

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Model (examples/sim/cruise_controller.sysml):

package Sim {
    attribute speed : ScalarValues::Real := 30;
    attribute key : ScalarValues::Boolean := true;

    action def logState;
    action def hold;

    state def Cruise {
        entry; then off;
        state off;
        state engaged;
        state holding;
        state slowing;
        transition engage first off accept Engage when key do logState then engaged;
        transition hold first engaged accept SpeedOK do hold then holding;
        transition slow first holding accept Decel when speed > 40 do logState then slowing;
        transition resume first slowing accept SpeedOK then holding;
        transition stop first holding accept Off when speed <= 5 then off;
        transition cancel first engaged accept Cancel then off;
    }
}

Interactive TUI:

sysmlpy sim examples/sim/cruise_controller.sysml

State machine Cruise — current: 'off'
  > off
    engaged
    holding
    slowing
transitions from here:
  0) Engage when key -> (target)  [guard: TRUE]
commands: <n> fire · <Trigger> fire · step · set name=value · values · log · q
> set speed=70
> Engage
State machine Cruise — current: 'engaged'
...

Scripted (for demos and CI):

sysmlpy sim examples/sim/cruise_controller.sysml \
    --run "Engage; SpeedOK; Decel; SpeedOK; Off; Cancel" --set speed=70

Engage: fired -> 'engaged'
SpeedOK: fired -> 'holding'
Decel: fired -> 'slowing'
SpeedOK: fired -> 'holding'
Off: blocked -> 'holding'      # speed=70, guard `speed <= 5` is false
Cancel: blocked -> 'holding'   # Cancel only leaves 'engaged'

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from sysmlpy import loads
from sysmlpy.sim import StateSimulator

sim = StateSimulator(model, focus="Cruise")
sim.state                     # 'off'
sim.available()               # [('Engage', 'key', True)] — (trigger, guard, passes now)
sim.send("Engage")            # True -> state 'engaged'
sim.set_value("speed", 70)    # what-if override for guards
sim.step()                    # fire the first enabled transition
sim.log                       # every fired/blocked attempt, with guard results
sim.reset()                   # back to the initial state, log cleared

docs.title: Semantics
docs.text:
• Initial state from entry; then X; (the official initial-point shorthand). Machines without one start in the first declared state (a note is reported).
  • Triggers (accept <Signal>) fire when sent; a trigger carried by several transitions from the current state falls through the guards in declaration order (first guard that holds wins).
  • Completion transitions (no accept) fire automatically on entering a state (UML run-to-completion) and manually via step().
  • Guards (when <expr>) evaluate against the model's attribute values (collect_values, pint Quantity-aware) plus set_value overrides; a guard that cannot evaluate blocks the transition and is logged.
  • Effects (do <action>) are logged as text — behavior references round-trip (do logState → logState), and the send/assignment forms surface their declarations (send Alert to logger, x := 5).
  • Composite states expand with qualified names (Composite.Sub): a transition targeting a composite enters its initial substate (UML default entry), the region runs its own transitions, and a transition declared on the composite applies from every substate — deeper transitions win the fall-through.

docs.title: Scope of the MVP
docs.text:
• Parallel regions raise SimulationError (top-level or inside a composite). Substates referenced by bare name from outside their region are flattened implicitly, with a note.
  • One machine per simulator (--focus picks which); parallel regions raise SimulationError for now.
  • Effects are logged, not executed; effect-side assignments (their target := value text is now available) would flow through set_value and are a follow-up. Composite regions and parallel regions are flat/raise for now (the descriptor carries the composites).

docs.title: Library choice
docs.text: Execution delegates to transitions (the sim extra). It builds machines from data at runtime — Machine(model=…, states=[…], transitions=[{...}]) — which is exactly the shape of the SysML-model → machine bridge, and its guards (conditions) and effects (before/after) map 1:1 onto the SysML guard/effect features. The runner-up, python-statemachine, prefers declarative class definitions, which is awkward for arbitrary parsed models; a hand-rolled kernel remains a fallback if deep SysML semantics (do-actions over time, after deadlines, history) outgrow it.

docs.title: SysML v2 Jupyter Magic Commands — Reference
docs.text:
Two implementations of notebook SysML exist in the ecosystem:

  1. The OMG Pilot Implementation kernel (org.omg.sysml.jupyter.kernel, Java/Xtext, installed via Miniconda from https://github.com/Systems-Modeling/SysML-v2-Pilot-Implementation) — a full Jupyter kernel where SysML is the language of the notebook itself.
  2. sysml_magic.py (this template) — an IPython extension providing a %%sysml cell magic in the ordinary Python kernel, backed by sysmlpy. Pure Python, no JVM.

This document records the official Pilot Implementation magic commands (extracted from SysMLInteractive.java and SysMLInteractiveHelp.java) and what this template's magic supports for each.

docs.title: Official Pilot Implementation commands
docs.text:
Magic Purpose (per %help <cmd> strings in the Pilot source) %help [<COMMAND>] List available commands, or detailed help on one. %eval [--target=<NAME>] <EXPR> Evaluate an expression, optionally in the scope of a named (fully qualified) element. %list [<QUERY>] With no argument, list all loaded library packages. With <QUERY> (a legal import name: N, N::*, N::**, optionally followed by a [filter]), list matching elements. %show [--style=<STYLE>] <NAME> Print the abstract syntax tree rooted at <NAME>. Styles: TREE (indented), JSON. %publish [-d] [--project=<P>] [--branch=<B>] <NAME> Publish the elements rooted at <NAME> to the model repository. -d includes derived properties. %viz [--view=<VIEW>] [--style=<STYLE>...] <NAME>... PlantUML visualization. Views: DEFAULT, TREE (≈BDD), INTERCONNECTION (≈IBD), STATE, ACTION, SEQUENCE, MIXED. Styles include LR, ortholine, … (delegated to SysML2PlantUMLStyle). %view [--render=<RENDERING>] [--style=<STYLE>...] <NAME> Render a view usage defined in the model itself. Renderings: same set as %viz views. %export <NAME> Write a JSON file of the AST rooted at <NAME>. %load [--id=<ID>] [--name=<N>] [--branch=<B>] [<NAME>] Download previously published models from the repository. %projects List projects in the repository (name + UUID). %repo [<BASE PATH>] Set/print the repository API base path used by %publish/%load/%projects. %exit (Console/REPL mode only) leave the interactive session.

The Pilot kernel additionally reads $ISYSML_API_BASE_PATH and $ISYSML_GRAPHVIZ_PATH environment variables (also settable via --api-base-path / --graphviz-path) to locate the repository API and the Graphviz dot binary used by %viz.

docs.title: sysml_magic support in this template
docs.text:
The ordinary-Python-kernel magic implements the interaction patterns that make sense client-side, backed by sysmlpy instead of the Eclipse/EMF stack. Repository-backed commands (%publish, %load, %projects, %repo) require the OMG API server and are out of scope; use the Pilot kernel if you need them.

Official command This template Notes (SysML cell) %%sysml [--reset] [--file PATH] [--show] Cell body is SysML source. Accumulates into a persistent model. Package members merge by (name, sysml_type): re-declared elements replace, others are preserved. %help %%sysml? / module docstring help(sysml_magic) or the docstrings. %list [<QUERY>] %sysml_list [NAME] No arg: top-level packages. With a name: exact-name matches at any depth. Richer queries: model.find(sysml_type='part', recursive=False) from Python. %show [--style] <NAME> %sysml_show NAME [--json] dump() tree text, or full JSON with --json. %viz [--view] [--style] <NAME> %sysml_viz NAME [--view V] Views: general, interconnection, action, package, tree (sysmlpy PlantUML generators). Output is PlantUML text; render with the PlantUML CLI/extension, or embed via a PlantUML server. %eval <EXPR> Python cells directly The model is a live Python object (model, alias _sysml); evaluate with plain Python. %view <NAME> not yet Requires sysmlpy View/Viewpoint rendering; planned. %export <NAME> %sysml_show NAME --json Prints JSON; redirect to a file if needed. %publish / %load / %projects / %repo not supported Requires the OMG API repository service. %exit n/a Jupyter manages the session.

docs.title: Session semantics
docs.text:
• The first %%sysml cell creates model and binds it into the notebook namespace (as model and _sysml).
  • Each subsequent cell is parsed fresh and merged into the session model at package-member granularity: a member with the same name and sysml_type replaces the old one; everything else is kept. So you can iterate on a single part definition in one cell without re-stating the rest of the package.
  • Parse errors are reported to stderr with line/column and do not discard the session model — fix and re-run the cell.
  • %%sysml --reset (or %sysml_reset) starts over from an empty model.
  • Semantic diagnostics from sysmlpy's analyzer run after each merge and surface as [semantic] [code] message on stderr.

docs.title: Known differences from the Pilot kernel
docs.text:
• Names must be matched exactly as declared (sysmlpy find); the Pilot kernel additionally supports filter expressions in [] after ::*.
  • %viz styles are limited to sysmlpy's PlantUML generator options (style="bw" etc.), not the full OMG style matrix.
  • No repository integration (publish/load/projects/repo).
  • Only %%sysml cells are SysML; everything else is Python. The Pilot kernel inverts this (everything is SysML unless it's a %... command).

Historical/reference material kept for provenance. docs.title: sysmlpy vs PySysML2: Comparison
docs.text:
A detailed comparison of two Python libraries for SysML v2 textual modeling.

Feature sysmlpy PySysML2 Version 0.31.3 0.1.1 Maintainer Jon Fox (mycr0ft) Keith Lucas (DAF Digital Transformation Office) License MIT Apache 2.0 Repository https://github.com/mycr0ft/sysmlpy https://github.com/DAF-Digital-Transformation-Office/PySysML2 Language Python 3.9+ Python 3.8+ Parser ANTLR4 (full SysML v2 grammar) ANTLR4 (subset grammar) Stars ~250+ ~60 Commits 1000+ 2 (initial commit + 1 update) Core source ~37K lines across 11 modules ~1.5K lines across 4 modules

docs.title: sysmlpy
docs.text:
Full SysML v2 / KerML metamodel via ANTLR4 grammar. 319 grammar classes in grammar/classes.py covering all SysML v2 constructs:

Structural: packages, parts, items, ports, interfaces, connections, flows (with flow definitions), attributes (with redefinition), enumerations, references, allocations, messages

Behavioral: actions (definition usage, shorthand, succession, decomposition), states (with transitions), calculations, constraints

Control flow: if/else, while loops, for loops, fork, join, decision, send, accept, terminate

Requirements & analysis: requirements, use cases, objectives, analysis cases, verification cases, trade studies

Views & cross-cutting: views (general, action flow, interconnection, state transition, package), viewpoints, concerns, metadata, renderings, individuals

Full round-trip: all 77 grammar tests pass (parse -> grammar object -> dump() -> re-parse -> identical)

# sysmlpy parsing examples
from sysmlpy import loads, parse, load_grammar

# Parse from string — returns Model
model = loads("""
    package Simple {
        part def Motor;
        part myMotor : Motor;
    }
""")

# Parse with error handling (never raises)
m, errors = parse("invalid syntax {{}")
# returns (None, [error lines])

# Raw dict access
d = load_grammar("part def A;")

docs.title: PySysML2
docs.text:
Partial SysML v2 grammar with ~15 element types, 4 relationship types:

Elements: package, part definition, attribute, comment, doc, import, include, item, objective, port, use case, connection end part

Relationships: connect, specializes, redefines, message

Not implemented (raise NotImplementedError): actor, about

Not covered at all: actions, states, constraints, calculations, flows (no flow def), interfaces, requirements, views/viewpoints, control flow, analysis cases, enumerations, references, allocations, messages (partially), metadata, renderings

# PySysML2 parsing examples
from pysysml2.modeling import Model

model = Model()
model.from_sysml2_file("model.sysml2")
# No string-based API; only file-based

# No load_grammar/loads equivalent — must write to file first
# No error handling API

docs.title: sysmlpy
docs.text:
Full programmatic construction of SysML models with type checking, unit support, and round-trip text generation:

from sysmlpy import Part, Item, Attribute, Action, Port, Connection, State, \
    Requirement, Case, Constraint, Calculation, Enumeration, ureg

# Structure
sensor = Part(name="sensor")
camera = Part(name="camera")
lens = Item(name="lens")
mass = Attribute(name="mass")
mass.set_value(100 * ureg.kilogram)
camera.add_child(mass)
sensor.add_child(camera)
sensor.add_child(lens)

print(sensor.dump())
# part sensor {
#     part camera {
#         attribute mass = 100 kg;
#     }
#     item lens;
# }

# Behavior
action = Action(definition=True, name='Focus')
action.add_input('scene', 'Scene')
action.add_output('image', 'Image')

# Ports & connections
port1 = Port(name='data')
port2 = Port(name='power')

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
sysmlpy provides comprehensive, production-grade SysML v2 support with full grammar coverage, programmatic model construction, semantic analysis, 14 PlantUML view types, 4 storage backends, ISQ unit validation, multi-file project support, and a complete standard library. It supports round-trip text output (dump()) from all grammar objects.

PySysML2 is a lightweight early-prototype focused on data-science-oriented model export (CSV, Excel, JSON, graphviz). It parses a subset of SysML v2 (~15 element types) into an anytree hierarchy and can export to pandas-friendly formats. It has no semantic analysis, no programmatic construction API, no round-trip text output, no unit validation, and no diagram generation beyond basic anytree graphviz trees.

Choose sysmlpy if you need: full SysML v2 modeling, diagram generation, semantic validation, multi-file projects, or programmatic model construction.

Choose PySysML2 if you need: a lightweight parse-to-DataFrame pipeline for simple SysML models with basic element types, and do not need round-trip, validation, diagrams, or behavioral elements.

The parse/analyze/round-trip engine is complete (§1–§4). The remaining work is the last mile between "correct toolkit" and "daily tool". Strategic framing: sysmlpy will not out-Cameo Cameo — the winnable position is headless SysML for the Python ecosystem: validation in CI, diagram/table generation in documentation pipelines, and models connected to Python-based analysis code.

Prioritized goals (tracked as checkboxes in TODO.md):

# Goal Gap today Effort 1 CLI: analyze + view commands with exit codes CLI is parse/format only; no severity-filtered lint output for CI days 2 Requirement traceability & verification coverage satisfy/verify/allocation usages parse but are never traversed: no coverage reports or verification matrices; no ReqIF 1–2 wks 3 JSON interchange format --json dumps the internal dict, not the SysML v2 spec's JSON interchange format 1–2 wks 4 Expression evaluator const_fold handles literals only; nothing binds attribute values (pint) into calc/constraint evaluation 2–3 wks 5 LSP server No editor integration; raw ANTLR error wording (SLL/LL parity, see TODO) 2–4 wks 6 Rendering without Java Views emit PlantUML source; rendering requires a Java toolchain. boxes covers state machines only 1–2 wks 7 Spreadsheet bridge Tabular views output text only; no CSV/XLSX export or attribute-value import days 8 Semantic model diff Nothing exists for review workflows ~1 wk 9 Validator depth ~10 OCL checks vs. hundreds in the spec incremental 10 Technical stubs Connector-end compatibility, *// unit derivation, SLL error parity, regex-based library extraction, Cayley parity scattered

Sequencing rationale: goals 1–3 are well-scoped on top of existing APIs (parse()/analyze() were deliberately built non-raising for exactly these consumers) and establish the CI-validation, traceability, and interop story. Goal 4 turns analyze() from "is this well-formed" into "does this model pass its own constraints" — the bridge to trade studies. Goal 5 rounds out the authoring experience.

docs.title: SysML v2 Reference Implementation — PlantUML Visual Design Analysis
Overview
docs.text: The official SysML v2 Pilot Implementation (org.omg.sysml.plantuml) generates PlantUML text from parsed SysML v2 models using a Visitor pattern in Java. It does not modify PlantUML's source code. Instead, it maps SysML v2 concepts to the closest available PlantUML syntax, accepting visual approximations and relying on stereotypes/legends for semantic clarity.

docs.title: 1. Element Box Shapes: Usage vs Definition
The Distinction
docs.text: In SysML v2, every structural element comes in two forms: - Definition (e.g., part def Wheel) — a classifier/type - Usage (e.g., part frontLeft : Wheel) — an instance/occurrence of a definition

docs.title: How the Reference Implementation Renders Them
docs.text:
Both are rendered using PlantUML's rectangle keyword. The visual distinction is achieved through stereotypes, not different shapes:

rectangle "Wheel" as E1 <<(D,brown) part def>>
rectangle "frontLeft" as E2 <<(P,limegreen) part>>

Key mechanism: styleString(Type typ) in SysML2PlantUMLText.java

  1. Determines the metaclass name from the EMF EClass (e.g., PartDefinition, PartUsage)
  2. Strips Definition → adds def suffix; strips Usage → no suffix
  3. Wraps in a stereotype with a colored icon letter:
  4. (D,brown) for Definitions
  5. (P,limegreen) for Parts (Usage)
  6. (P,blue) for Ports
  7. (B,green) for Items
  8. (U,orange) for generic Usages
  9. (B,lemonchiffon) for Behaviors
  10. (F,yellow) for Features

docs.title: Rounded Corners
docs.text:
The reference implementation uses PlantUML's skinparam roundcorner to give all boxes rounded corners uniformly. There is no distinction in corner radius between Usage and Definition — both get the same roundcorner value (typically 20).

skinparam roundcorner 20

docs.title: 3. Redefinition Decoration on Features
docs.text:
When decoratedRedefined style is enabled, redefined features get inline decoration:

"featureName" as E1 <<(U,orange) feature>>
E1 :> redefinedFeatureName

The code in VStructure.java adds \n//:>>redefinedFeature// as a note inside the box, or uses the PlantUML icon <&bar-trig> prefix with the redefined name struck through:

<&bar-trig> featureName <s>redefinedFeatureName</s>

docs.title: 4. Compartment Rendering
docs.text:
The reference implementation supports compartments inside boxes for: - Attributes - Ports - Connections - Requirements - States - Actions

These are rendered as PlantUML compartment sections within rectangle or component blocks:

rectangle "Wheel" as E1 <<part def>> {
  attribute radius : LengthValue
  port hub : PortDefinition
}

docs.title: 5. Style System
docs.text: The reference implementation defines three primary styles:

docs.title: Standard B&W (STDBW)
docs.text:
skin sysmlbw
skinparam monochrome true
skinparam wrapWidth 300
hide circle

docs.title: Standard Color (STDCOLOR)
docs.text:
skin sysmlc
skinparam wrapWidth 300
hide circle
Plus custom relationship styling: - Connectors: -[thickness=3,#blue]- - BindingConnector: -[thickness=5,#red]- - FeatureValue: -[thickness=5,#red]-

docs.title: PlantUML Style (PLANTUML)
docs.text: Uses standard PlantUML defaults with colored stereotypes.

docs.title: Direction & Layout Options
docs.text:
• TB — top to bottom direction
  • LR — left to right direction
  • POLYLINE — polyline line type
  • ORTHOLINE — orthogonal line type

docs.title: 6. Multiplicity
docs.text:
Multiplicity can be shown in three modes: - EDGE — on the relationship arrow (default) - NODE — inside the element box - BOTH — on both - NONE — hidden

Implicit multiplicities are hidden by default unless implicitMultiplicity is enabled.

docs.title: 7. Key Takeaways for Our Implementation
docs.text:
1. No PlantUML modification needed — the reference impl uses only standard PlantUML syntax
  2. Stereotypes carry semantic weight — the colored (Letter,color) icons are the primary visual differentiator between element types
  3. Arrow approximations are accepted — --||> for redefinition, --:|> for typing
  4. Thickness + color differentiate relationships — binding is thick red, connectors are blue
  5. Rounded corners are uniform — no shape difference between Usage and Definition
  6. Compartments show internal structure — attributes, ports, etc. inside boxes
  7. A legend is essential — without it, the approximations are ambiguous

docs.title: v0.46.0 — Structured Expression Capture (Capture-Don't-Evaluate)
docs.text: Status: - Phase 0 (prerequisite) — DONE in v0.48.0: assert constraint / constraint / calc / state / action / requirement / satisfy / allocation usages inside part def, item def, etc. bodies now survive Part.load_from_grammar into the public-API tree. 10 regression tests in tests/grammar_test.py::*v046_phase0*. - Phase 1 (expression refactor) — DONE in v0.52.0: visitor now emits a structured expression dict with operators captured at the correct layer, using a precedence-climbing pass to recover the correct operator order from the left-associative ANTLR parse. 10 regression tests in tests/grammar_test.py::*v046_phase1 (binary equality, invocation, feature chain, arithmetic precedence, unary minus, not operator, logical and/or (text-preservation fallback), conditional ternary (layer-presence), range, structural non-collapse). Known limitations: - and/or/xor/implies fall back to text preservation (the grammar classes use list-based operand/operator fields that don't fit the chain layout). - a.b field access falls back to text preservation (the grammar class lacks a FeatureChainExpression that BaseExpression can read). - The grammar's IF ? : ternary form is not currently parseable inside calc bodies (known grammar limitation). Author: Context from issue #3 triage + codebase investigation. Target release: v0.48.0 (Phase 0), v0.52.0 (Phase 1) Estimated effort: ~1 week (see §8).

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
Today, _visit_owned_expression (src/sysmlpy/antlr_visitor.py:10557) collapses every non-literal expression into a single FeatureReferenceMember whose memberElement is a QualifiedName with the whole expression text as a single name part. Example:

assert constraint { radius == zero }
# visitor emits:
#   FeatureReferenceExpression
#     FeatureReferenceMember
#       QualifiedName { names: ["radius==zero"] }   # ← entire text, structure lost

The wrapping EqualityExpression / AdditiveExpression / … chain in _wrap_expression_layers is emitted with empty operator/operand arrays for every binary layer, so the operator is never captured. Round-trip works only because QualifiedName.dump() returns the raw text verbatim.

This makes a future name resolver infeasible: a resolver needs individually addressable FeatureReferenceExpression nodes (one per identifier) so it can look each up in the symbol table. With the current lossy collapse, the resolver would have to re-parse raw text — duplicating grammar work and drifting from the ANTLR grammar.

A second, related bug blocks testing: assert constraint inside a part def body is dropped by Part.load_from_grammar in src/sysmlpy/usage.py:782. That dispatch handles PartDefinition / ItemUsage / AttributeUsage / etc. but has no branch for AssertConstraintUsage / ConstraintUsage / CalculationUsage. The visitor emits the assert constraint correctly; the grammar classes construct it correctly; usage.py discards it when building the public-API Part tree. So model.dump() silently omits every assert constraint inside a part. This must be fixed first so expression-capture tests can even observe the round-trip.

docs.title: 2. Goal
docs.text:
Replace the lossy single-FeatureReferenceMember collapse with a structured expression dict that preserves operator structure, so a future v0.47+ name resolver can walk identifiers individually.

In scope: - Prerequisite: plumb AssertConstraintUsage / ConstraintUsage / CalculationUsage / StateUsage / ActionUsage through Part.load_from_grammar so they survive into the public-API Part.children. - Refactor _visit_owned_expression to walk the ANTLR ownedExpression subtree and emit per-rule dicts keyed on the expression kind (BinaryExpression, InvocationExpression, FeatureChainExpression, LiteralInteger, LiteralReal, LiteralString, LiteralBoolean, FeatureReferenceExpression, MetadataAccessExpression, ConstructorExpression, CastExpression, ConditionalExpression, UnaryExpression, ParenthesizedExpression, IfExpression). - Add matching grammar classes in grammar/classes.py for any new dict shapes that don't already have a class (most already exist — see §4). - Public API: Model.find_expressions() helper that walks assertConstraintUsage / calculationUsage / requirementUsage and yields (constraint, expression) pairs. - Documentation: README + STATUS + CHANGELOG.

Out of scope (deferred to v0.47+): - Name resolution (looking up identifiers in the symbol table). - Type checking (verifying operand types are compatible). - OCL evaluation (evaluating the expression to a value). - Constraint-body semantic checks (the "check" half of "parse + check").

docs.title: 3. Architecture: the capture layer
docs.text:
SysML text
  → ANTLR4 parse tree (ownedExpression context tree)
  → _visit_owned_expression (REFACTORED)
  → structured OwnedExpression dict
  → grammar/classes.py (OwnedExpression / ConditionalExpression / …)
  → dump() / get_definition() round-trip
  → (future v0.47+) semantic.py walks the structured dict, resolves names

The refactor touches only the visitor emission and the grammar-class construction. Everything downstream (the OwnedExpression / ConditionalExpression / EqualityExpression / … class hierarchy in grammar/classes.py:5539-6350) already exists and already round-trips — the problem is that the visitor never fills the operator/operand arrays, so the classes get empty data.

Today they just join operands (no operator text), because the visitor never fills the operator arrays. docs.title: Phase 0 — Prerequisite: assert constraint survives Part.load_from_grammar
docs.text:
File: src/sysmlpy/usage.py (Usage.load_from_grammar, line 782).

The children-dispatch loop (lines ~920-1078) handles PartDefinition, ItemDefinition, PartUsage, ItemUsage, AttributeUsage, StructureUsageElement, StructureDefinitionElement, Definition. It does NOT handle AssertConstraintUsage, ConstraintUsage, CalculationUsage, StateUsage, ActionUsage, RequirementUsage, SatisfyRequirementUsage, FlowConnectionUsage (as children of a part), ConnectionUsage (as child of part), InterfaceUsage, etc.

Fix: add a branch for each missing usage kind. For AssertConstraintUsage / ConstraintUsage / CalculationUsage, construct a Constraint (or Calculation) public-API object, set .grammar = inner_element, extract name from the declaration if present, set .parent = self, append to self.children. Mirror the pattern already used at the package level in definition.py:1269-1290.

Risk: Part.dump() and Attribute.usage_dump() rebuild the body via _get_definition(child="DefinitionBody") — need to verify the rebuilt dict includes the assert constraint. If Constraint doesn't have a _get_definition that emits the right DefinitionBodyItem shape, the round-trip will drop it. Check Constraint._get_definition (in usage.py) and extend if needed.

Tests (failing-first, commit before the visitor refactor): - test_assert_constraint_survives_part_def_load_gh3_prereq: part def W { attribute r; assert constraint { r == 0 } } → model.dump() contains assert constraint. - test_constraint_usage_survives_part_def_load_gh3_prereq: part def W { constraint c { r == 0 } } → model.dump() contains constraint c. - test_calculation_usage_survives_part_def_load_gh3_prereq: part def W { calc mass { sum(parts.mass) } } → model.dump() contains calc mass.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Visitor refactor: structured expression emission
docs.text:
File: src/sysmlpy/antlr_visitor.py.

Replace _visit_owned_expression (line 10557) with a dispatcher that walks the ANTLR ownedExpression context tree and fills the existing expression chain with real operator/operand data instead of empty arrays.

Key insight: the ANTLR ownedExpression rule is left-recursive with operator precedence (see SysMLv2Parser.g4:22-62). ANTLR parses radius == zero as:

ownedExpression
  : ownedExpression EQ_EQ ownedExpression    # the == alternative
      ↳ lhs: ownedExpression (baseExpression)
      ↳ rhs: ownedExpression (baseExpression)

ANTLR's Python runtime exposes this as: oe_ctx.getChildCount() == 3, oe_ctx.getChild(0) is the lhs ownedExpression, oe_ctx.getChild(1) is the EQ_EQ terminal, oe_ctx.getChild(2) is the rhs ownedExpression. For unary prefix (-x, not x): getChildCount() == 2, getChild(0) is the operator terminal, getChild(1) is the operand. For the base case (baseExpression): oe_ctx.baseExpression() is non-null.

New helper functions (add near _visit_owned_expression):

def _emit_expression(oe_ctx):
    """Walk an ownedExpression context and return a structured OwnedExpression
    dict. Dispatches on ANTLR child shape: binary operator, unary operator,
    conditional (if/then/else), or base expression."""
    ...

def _emit_binary_expression(lhs_ctx, op_terminal, rhs_ctx):
    """Fill the EqualityExpression / RelationalExpression / AdditiveExpression /
    MultiplicativeExpression / ExponentiationExpression / RangeExpression /
    AndExpression / OrExpression / XorExpression / ImpliesExpression /
    NullCoalescingExpression / ConditionalExpression layers with real operator
    and operand data."""
    ...

def _emit_unary_expression(op_terminal, operand_ctx):
    """Fill the UnaryExpression layer with the operator and operand."""
    ...

def _emit_conditional_expression(if_ctx, then_ctx, else_ctx):
    """Fill the ConditionalExpression layer with condition/then/else."""
    ...

def _emit_base_expression(base_ctx):
    """Dispatch a baseExpression to the right primary: literal, feature
    reference, invocation, constructor, body expression, cast, or
    parenthesized expression."""
    ...

Strategy for _emit_binary_expression: the existing _wrap_expression_layers builds the empty chain. Reuse it as a skeleton, but instead of passing a single primary_expression at the bottom, walk the lhs and rhs recursively and splice them into the right operator layer. Map the operator terminal to the layer:

Operator terminal(s) Expression layer (existing class) EQ_EQ, BANG_EQ, EQ_EQ_EQ, BANG_EQ_EQ EqualityExpression LT, GT, LE, GE RelationalExpression PLUS, MINUS AdditiveExpression STAR, SLASH, PERCENT MultiplicativeExpression STAR_STAR, CARET ExponentiationExpression DOT_DOT RangeExpression AMP AndExpression PIPE OrExpression XOR XorExpression IMPLIES ImpliesExpression QUESTION_QUESTION NullCoalescingExpression IF / QUESTION / ELSE (ternary) ConditionalExpression

For each binary node, emit: 

{
  "name": "<LayerName>Expression",       # e.g. "EqualityExpression"
  "operator": [op_text],                 # e.g. ["=="]
  "operand": [lhs_dict, rhs_dict],        # two operands, recursively structured
  # ...nested layers below this one, filled by recursing into lhs/rhs...
}

Critical: keep the existing nested-layer structure (the ConditionalExpression → NullCoalescingExpression → ImpliesExpression → … → PrimaryExpression chain) so existing grammar classes still work. The change is that the operator/operand arrays are now populated with real data instead of empty.

Backstop: if _emit_expression can't recognize a shape (defensive — should not happen for valid SysML), fall back to the existing _make_feature_reference_primary(text) path. Print a [expression] unhandled X warning (mirrors the AGENTS.md catch-all pattern). This preserves the graceful-fallback contract.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Grammar class dump() fixes
docs.text:
File: src/sysmlpy/grammar/classes.py.

The existing dump() methods on EqualityExpression, RelationalExpression, AdditiveExpression, MultiplicativeExpression, ExponentiationExpression, UnaryExpression, ConditionalExpression currently join operands with no operator text (because the visitor never filled operators). After Phase 1, the visitor fills operators, so dump() must emit lhs OP rhs.

Pattern (apply to each binary-expression class): 

def dump(self):
    parts = []
    for i, operand in enumerate(self.operands):
        parts.append(operand.dump())
        if i < len(self.operator):
            parts.append(self.operator[i])   # the operator string
    return " ".join(parts)   # or "" .join, matching existing whitespace

Audit each class's existing dump() and adjust. Verify against the failing-first tests from Phase 0 + new expression regression tests.

For UnaryExpression: 

def dump(self):
    if self.operator:
        return f"{self.operator} {self.operand.dump()}"   # or no space, per grammar
    return self.operand.dump()

For ConditionalExpression (if/then/else): 

def dump(self):
    # if cond ? then : else  →  SysML syntax is "if cond then x else y"
    # Verify the exact SysML v2 syntax for conditional expressions.

Risk: whitespace. Existing tests use strip_ws(text) == strip_ws(dump()), so whitespace differences are tolerated. But new tests should use exact whitespace where it matters for readability.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Public API
docs.text:
File: src/sysmlpy/__init__.py (or a new src/sysmlpy/expressions.py module, exported from __init__.py).

Add: 

def find_expressions(model) -> list[tuple[Any, Any]]:
    """Walk a model and yield (container, expression) pairs for every
    assert constraint, constraint usage, and calculation usage body.

    Each `expression` is the structured OwnedExpression dict (the visitor
    output). A future name resolver (v0.47+) can consume this directly.

    Returns
    -------
    list[tuple[Any, dict]]
        List of (container_element, expression_dict) pairs.
    """
    ...

Walk the model: for each Part / Attribute / Constraint / Calculation / Requirement in model.children (recursively), find AssertConstraintUsage / ConstraintUsage / CalculationUsage in .grammar.body (or .grammar.definition.body), drill into ResultExpressionMember.ownedRelatedElement, yield the pair.

Tests: - test_find_expressions_returns_structured_gh3: for a model with assert constraint { radius == zero }, find_expressions(model) returns a list whose first element's expression dict contains an EqualityExpression with operator: ["=="] and two FeatureReferenceExpression operands (radius, zero).

docs.title: Phase 4 — Regression tests
docs.text:
File: tests/grammar_test.py (add at the end, near the issue #3 tests).

Add these failing-first tests, commit them BEFORE the refactor so they document the expected end state:

def test_expression_capture_binary_regression_gh3_capture():
    """`radius == zero` must round-trip with the operator captured."""
    text = """package P {
        part def W {
            attribute r;
            assert constraint { r == zero }
        }
    }"""
    a = loads(text)
    dumped = classtree(a).dump()
    assert "==" in dumped, f"binary operator lost; got: {dumped!r}"
    assert "r" in dumped and "zero" in dumped


def test_expression_capture_invocation_regression_gh3_capture():
    """`size(edges) == 18` must round-trip with the invocation captured."""
    text = """package P {
        part def Shape {
            attribute edges;
            assert constraint { size(edges) == 18 }
        }
    }"""
    a = loads(text)
    dumped = classtree(a).dump()
    assert "size(edges)" in dumped or "size ( edges )" in dumped
    assert "==" in dumped and "18" in dumped


def test_expression_capture_chain_regression_gh3_capture():
    """`wheel1.mass` must round-trip as a feature chain, not raw text."""
    text = """package P {
        part def Vehicle {
            part wheel1 { attribute mass; }
            assert constraint { wheel1.mass > 0 }
        }
    }"""
    a = loads(text)
    dumped = classtree(a).dump()
    assert "wheel1" in dumped and "mass" in dumped
    assert ">" in dumped and "0" in dumped


def test_expression_capture_arithmetic_regression_gh3_capture():
    """`a + b * c` must round-trip with precedence preserved."""
    text = """package P {
        part def E {
            attribute a; attribute b; attribute c;
            assert constraint { a + b * c == 0 }
        }
    }"""
    a = loads(text)
    dumped = classtree(a).dump()
    assert "+" in dumped and "*" in dumped and "==" in dumped


def test_expression_capture_unary_regression_gh3_capture():
    """`-x` and `not flag` must round-trip with the unary operator captured."""
    text = """package P {
        part def E {
            attribute x; attribute flag;
            assert constraint { -x == 0 and not flag }
        }
    }"""
    a = loads(text)
    dumped = classtree(a).dump()
    assert "-" in dumped and "not" in dumped

Also add a structural test (not just text round-trip) to lock in the dict shape so a future resolver has something to walk:

def test_expression_dict_has_equality_layer_gh3_capture():
    """The visitor must emit a populated EqualityExpression, not an empty one
    with the whole text collapsed into a FeatureReferenceMember."""
    from sysmlpy.antlr_parser import parse
    from sysmlpy.antlr_visitor import _visit_root_namespace_dict
    text = """package P {
        part def W {
            attribute r;
            assert constraint { r == zero }
        }
    }"""
    d = _visit_root_namespace_dict(parse(text))

    def find_first(node, target):
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            if node.get("name") == target:
                return node
            for v in node.values():
                r = find_first(v, target) if isinstance(v, (dict, list)) else None
                if r: return r
        elif isinstance(node, list):
            for it in node:
                r = find_first(it, target) if isinstance(it, (dict, list)) else None
                if r: return r
        return None

    eq = find_first(d, "EqualityExpression")
    assert eq is not None, "EqualityExpression layer missing entirely"
    assert len(eq.get("operator", [])) >= 1, \
        f"EqualityExpression has no operator; got: {eq!r}"
    assert eq["operator"][0] == "==", \
        f"EqualityExpression operator is not '=='; got: {eq['operator']!r}"

docs.title: 6. Risk mitigations
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Existing strip_ws(text) == strip_ws(dump()) tests break Each emitter preserves child text via getText() or by recursing into structured children. Whitespace behavior shouldn't change. If a test breaks, STOP. Deep operator precedence double-emits Write the deeply-nested test (a + b * c == 0) FIRST, before refactoring. Commit it as the regression bar. 354 grammar classes — adding new ones is small Audit first; most classes already exist. Only add what's missing. Part.load_from_grammar prerequisite fix breaks other tests The fix only ADDS branches for previously-dropped usage kinds; it doesn't change existing branches. Existing tests for parts/items/attributes are unaffected. dump() whitespace for binary operators differs from source Tolerated by strip_ws comparison. Document in STATUS.md. The visitor refactor is large Keep _wrap_expression_layers as the skeleton builder; only change what gets spliced into the operator/operand arrays. Mechanical change. Conformance baseline shifts Must stay at 118/123 with byte-identical failures. If it shifts, STOP.

docs.title: 7. What this enables (v0.47+)
docs.text:
A name resolver becomes feasible because every name reference inside an expression is now an individually-addressable FeatureReferenceExpression (with its FeatureChainExpression chain) rather than buried inside raw text.

v0.47+ name resolver sketch: 1. Walk assertConstraintUsage → calculationBody → resultExpressionMember → ownedExpression (recursive). 2. At each FeatureReferenceExpression, resolve the qualifiedName against the SymbolTable (already built by semantic.py). 3. At each FeatureChainExpression, resolve the source's type, then resolve each chain step on that type (extending _check_feature_chaining_compatible in semantic.py:1800). 4. Emit SemanticIssues for unresolved names.

v0.48+ type checker: verify operand types are compatible for each binary operator (e.g. == requires matching types, + requires numeric types).

v0.49+ OCL evaluation: evaluate the expression to a value (for assert constraint verification).

This is what gets you from "parse-clean but not checked" to "parse-clean AND names checked". Type-checking / OCL evaluation remain out of scope for v0.47.

docs.title: XText Reference Implementation — Insights for sysmlpy
docs.text: Status: Research notes (not a release) Author: Comparative analysis of the OMG SysML v2 Pilot Implementation Repository studied: https://github.com/Systems-Modeling/SysML-v2-Pilot-Implementation

docs.title: 1. The OMG Pilot Implementation is XText-based
docs.text:
The OMG SysML v2 Pilot Implementation is built on Eclipse XText (a Java/Eclipse framework for domain-specific languages). XText's grammar is a superset of ANTLR with semantic-action syntax ({Model::Class.feature = current}) for directly constructing the AST model during parsing.

The expression grammar lives in: - org.omg.kerml.expressions.xtext/src/org/omg/kerml/expressions/xtext/KerMLExpressions.xtext - org.omg.sysml.xtext/src/org/omg/sysml/xtext/SysML.xtext

SysML.xtext imports org.omg.kerml.expressions.xtext.KerMLExpressions (line: grammar org.omg.sysml.xtext.SysML with org.omg.kerml.expressions.xtext.KerMLExpressions).

docs.title: 2. The OMG grammar HAS proper precedence (per-operator rules)
docs.text:
The OMG XText grammar expresses each operator level as a separate grammar rule with a clear precedence cascade. This is the canonical, correct way to handle precedence in XText/ANTLR.

OwnedExpression → ConditionalExpression
ConditionalExpression → NullCoalescingExpression | 'if' cond '?' then 'else' else
NullCoalescingExpression → ImpliesExpression ( '??' ImpliesExpressionReference )*
ImpliesExpression → OrExpression ( 'implies' OrExpressionReference )*
OrExpression → XorExpression ( '|' | 'or' XorExpressionReference )*
XorExpression → AndExpression ( 'xor' AndExpression )*
AndExpression → EqualityExpression ( '&' | 'and' EqualityExpressionReference )*
EqualityExpression → ClassificationExpression ( '==' | '!=' | '===' | '!==' )*
ClassificationExpression → RelationalExpression ( 'hastype' | 'istype' | '@' | 'as' type )?
RelationalExpression → RangeExpression ( '<' | '>' | '<=' | '>=' )*
RangeExpression → AdditiveExpression ( '..' AdditiveExpression )?
AdditiveExpression → MultiplicativeExpression ( '+' | '-' )*                    [left-assoc]
MultiplicativeExpression → ExponentiationExpression ( '*' | '/' | '%' )*          [left-assoc]
ExponentiationExpression → UnaryExpression ( '**' | '^' ExponentiationExpression )?   [right-assoc via ?]
UnaryExpression → ( '+' | '-' | '~' | 'not' ) ExtentExpression | ExtentExpression
ExtentExpression → 'all' type | PrimaryExpression
PrimaryExpression → BaseExpression ( '.' FeatureChainMember ( '[' ']' | '#' '(' ')' | '->' ... )* )*
BaseExpression → NullExpression | LiteralExpression | FeatureReferenceExpression
                | MetadataAccessExpression | InvocationExpression | ConstructorExpression
                | BodyExpression | '(' SequenceExpression ')'

docs.title: Key design choices in the OMG grammar
docs.text:
1. Same-precedence operators are merged in a single ( op operand )* loop with left-associativity. E.g. + and - are both at the additive level: 

    AdditiveExpression → MultiplicativeExpression ( ('+' | '-') MultiplicativeExpression )*

  2. Right-associative operators use ( op level )? (single optional op): 

    ExponentiationExpression → UnaryExpression ( ('**' | '^') ExponentiationExpression )?

  3. "Reference" variants wrap lower-precedence expressions as cross-references. The trick: when an operator's operand needs to be at a LOWER binding level (e.g., and taking an or-level operand), the operand is wrapped in <X>Reference which holds a membership/relationship to the lower-level expression. This produces the correct semantic structure for the AST.

Example from the OMG grammar: 

AndExpression → EqualityExpression ( ('&' EqualityExpression | 'and' EqualityExpressionReference) )*
                                                                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
The keyword form and takes an EqualityExpressionReference (a membership relationship) instead of a direct EqualityExpression. The membership relationship is how the AST preserves the source-level grouping.

  1. XText semantic actions attach the operator and operand to the current expression being built. Example: 
    AdditiveExpression returns SysML::Expression :
    MultiplicativeExpression ( {SysML::OperatorExpression.operand += current}
                               operator = AdditiveOperator operand += MultiplicativeExpression )*
;
    The {...} block runs after the LHS is matched, creating an OperatorExpression model element with operand set to the LHS and then assigning operator and the next operand to it.

docs.title: 3. The daltskin auto-generated ANTLR4 grammar has a precedence bug
docs.text:
The vendored grammar in src/sysmlpy/grammar/antlr4/SysMLv2Parser.g4 was auto-generated by daltskin/sysml-v2-grammar. The daltskin README states:

"Transform — Converts to ANTLR4 with precedence-climbing expressions, keyword extraction, and spec-ambiguity patches"

But the actual generated grammar has ALL operators collapsed into a SINGLE ownedExpression rule (line 22 in the vendored file):

ownedExpression
    : IF ownedExpression QUESTION ownedExpression ELSE ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression QUESTION_QUESTION ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression IMPLIES ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression OR ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression AND ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression XOR ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression PIPE ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression AMP ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression ( EQ_EQ | BANG_EQ | EQ_EQ_EQ | BANG_EQ_EQ) ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression ( LT | GT | GT | LE | GE) ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression DOT_DOT ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression ( PLUS | MINUS) ownedExpression
    | ownedExpression ( STAR | SLASH | PERCENT) ownedExpression
    | <assoc = right> ownedExpression ( STAR_STAR | CARET) ownedExpression
    | ( PLUS | MINUS | TILDE | NOT) ownedExpression
    | ...
    ;

This is a flat list — all operators are at the same precedence level. ANTLR4 resolves this with left-association and greedy matching: when a parser is at a ownedExpression choice-point and sees a + b * c, it consumes a + b (because the LHS of the + alternative greedily takes as much as possible), then sees * next which matches the * alternative, so the parse is (a + b) * c. The mathematically correct parse is a + (b * c) because * binds tighter than +, but the grammar doesn't enforce that.

This is the root cause of the precedence issue documented in docs/v0.46.0_expression_capture_plan.md and worked around in the visitor with the precedence-climbing pass added in v0.52.0.

docs.title: 4. The fix: regenerate (or patch) the grammar with per-precedence rules
docs.text: The cleanest fix is to regenerate the grammar with the per-precedence structure the OMG grammar uses. Two paths:

docs.title: Path A: Regenerate from daltskin (preferred)
docs.text:
File an issue / PR on https://github.com/daltskin/sysml-v2-grammar asking them to apply the "precedence-climbing expressions" transform they document. Their scripts/generate_grammar.py has an apply_patches() method that should be updated to generate per-precedence rules.

Once the grammar is regenerated, the sysmlpy visitor can be simplified back to a straightforward recursive-descent emit (no precedence-climbing needed in the visitor because the grammar does it).

docs.title: Path B: Patch the vendored grammar manually
docs.text:
Patch src/sysmlpy/grammar/antlr4/SysMLv2Parser.g4 to split the ownedExpression rule into the per-precedence rules shown in §2. This requires regenerating the Python ANTLR parser from the patched grammar:

java -jar antlr-4.13.2-complete.jar -Xexact-output-dir \
    -o src/sysmlpy/antlr \
    -visitor -listener -Dlanguage=Python3 \
    src/sysmlpy/grammar/antlr4/SysMLv2Lexer.g4 \
    src/sysmlpy/grammar/antlr4/SysMLv2Parser.g4

After the grammar fix, the visitor's precedence-climbing pass can be removed (replaced with straightforward recursive-descent emit) and the chain layout will match the grammar class layout exactly.

docs.title: 5. Why sysmlpy works today anyway (v0.52.0)
docs.text:
Even with the grammar precedence bug, sysmlpy v0.52.0's Phase 1 expression capture works because the visitor does its own precedence-climbing pass (_find_split_index / _build_binary_chain / _splice_operator / _add_op_to_layer / _embed_rhs_higher_ops in antlr_visitor.py). The pass: 1. Walks the ANTLR parse tree 2. Finds the lowest-precedence operator in the children 3. Re-arranges the structured chain so operators are at their correct binding-power layer 4. Embeds rhs's higher-layer operators when re-arranging

This duplicates what a correct grammar would do automatically. The grammar fix would let us remove ~300 lines of visitor code.

docs.title: 6. Concrete v0.53.0 work plan (if/when we want the grammar fix)
docs.text:
1. Patch the vendored grammar (Path B above) to add per-precedence rules for ownedExpression.
  2. Regenerate the ANTLR Python parser with the patched grammar.
  3. Run conformance tests to verify the new grammar still passes 118/123.
  4. Simplify the visitor by removing the precedence-climbing helpers (_PRECEDENCE_RANK, _OPERATOR_TO_LAYER, _find_split_index, _splice_operator, _add_op_to_layer, _embed_rhs_higher_ops, _embed_layer_at_path, _unwrap_to_layer, _rhs_top_op_layer, _rhs_has_higher_op, _LAYER_PATHS, _LAYER_OP_FIELDS, _LAYER_TO_OPERATORS, etc.).
  5. Re-run the test suite to verify all 143 grammar tests + 11 phase1 tests still pass without the precedence-climbing pass.
  6. Document the change in CHANGELOG as "v0.53.0 — fix grammar precedence; remove visitor-side precedence-climbing".
  7. Submit the grammar patch upstream to daltskin/sysml-v2-grammar so other ANTLR4-based SysML v2 consumers can benefit.

docs.title: 4. Compartment Alternative
docs.text:
Since rectangle { ... } compartments don't work, use PlantUML's class syntax for elements that need internal structure:

class "Wheel" as WheelDef {
  +radius : LengthValue
  +pressure : PressureValue
  +hubPort : Port
}

Or use notes adjacent to elements:

rectangle "Wheel" as W <<part def>>
note right of W
  radius : LengthValue
  pressure : PressureValue
  hubPort : Port
end note

docs.title: 5. Verdict: Acceptable Approximations
docs.text:
The PlantUML approximations are visually acceptable for engineering documentation when accompanied by a legend. The key relationships are distinguishable:

  • Binding (thick red line) is unmistakable
  • Composite vs Shared (filled vs hollow diamond) is exact
  • Typing (colon + arrow) is recognizable
  • Specialization (block arrow) is standard UML
  • Flow/Dependency (dotted arrows) are conventional

The main gaps (open vs filled arrowheads, slash vs double-bar) are semantic distinctions that matter to SysML v2 purists but are tolerable approximations for most audiences when documented in a legend.
